hook: In 1975 the world had 8 cities of 10 million people or more. In 2025 it had 33, and the largest, Jakarta in Indonesia, held nearly 42 million people (UN DESA, World Urbanization Prospects 2025). At the same time, many cities in the United States grew mostly outward, as families moved to suburbs and offices followed them. Cities are growing bigger in some places and wider in others.

options: A rise in the share of a population living in cities
The spread of farming into new regions
A fall in a city's population
The growth of villages into towns
prereq.why: Urbanization is about the share of people who live in cities, not just the number.

options: Contact between places falls as the distance between them grows
Places far apart trade more than places close together
Maps lose accuracy far from the equator
prereq.why: The farther apart two places are, the less they usually interact.

figure.caption: A large metro area: an old central city, suburbs, an edge city where highways meet, a boomburb and exurbs among farms.

chain.cause: Rural-to-urban migration and natural increase run high in many lower- and middle-income countries
chain.effect: their largest cities pass 10 million people and become megacities

chain.cause: After 1945, US highways, cheap home loans and cars made long commutes easy
chain.effect: families moved from central cities to suburbs: suburbanization

chain.cause: Homes spread at low density across former farmland
chain.effect: the metro area sprawls, and most trips need a car

chain.cause: Offices and stores follow workers and shoppers to the suburbs
chain.effect: edge cities grow where highways meet, and boomburbs and exurbs grow beyond them

ideas: A megacity has 10 million people or more; a metacity has 20 million or more. These are conventions, and a city's count depends on where its edge is drawn.
Most megacities are in Asia (19 of 33 in 2025, UN DESA), and most new ones are growing in lower- and middle-income countries.
Suburbanization is the movement of people and jobs from central cities to the surrounding suburbs. Low-density spread across the land is urban sprawl.

An edge city is a suburban center of offices and stores with more jobs than homes. An exurb is a rural-looking area beyond the suburbs where commuters live. A boomburb is a fast-growing suburb that has become a large city of its own.

misconception.wrong: An edge city is just a big suburb where people live.
misconception.right: An edge city is a job center: office towers, malls and hotels, usually at a highway junction, with more jobs than bedrooms. Tysons, Virginia, outside Washington, D.C., is an example. A suburb where most people live and leave each morning for work is not an edge city.

summary: Megacities (10 million or more) and metacities (20 million or more) are multiplying, mostly in Asia and Africa. In the United States and other high-income countries, cities spread outward instead: suburbanization and sprawl produced edge cities (suburban job centers), boomburbs (fast-growing suburban cities) and exurbs (commuter homes among farms).
